messages:
alex: Kicking off onboarding for zh-30b-intl. Need quick pre-dedicated checks: confirm weights location, tokenizer oddities (CJK vs ASCII punctuation), RoPE scaling strategy for long contexts, sliding-window stride effects, and KV-cache shape for MQA. Who can take parts? :wave:

priya: I can take tokenizer + basic validation. Where are the weights stored and what's the tokenizer format?

alex: Weights: s3://rw-models/zh-30b/int_v1/ (private). Export manifest included, sha256: 3f9a1cb9... Tokenizer: SentencePiece file spm_zh_30b.model, mixed CJK+latin tokens.

jamal: Noted. Quick repro of tokenizer quirk: mixed ASCII comma vs fullwidth comma changes tokenization boundaries which breaks prefix cache hits. Example: "\u4eca\u5929, I went" vs "\u4eca\u5929\uff0c I went". I'll attach tiny script in the PR.

maya: For RoPE, I want to validate we can use linear interpolation (our rope_scaling module). Proposal for runtime config:
```
rope:
  method: "interp_linear"
  base_len: 2048
  scale: 2.0  # target ~4096
```
Are our CUDA kernels tolerant of the rope table being resampled? env = cuda12 + q8 runtime.

tina: Important: Is this model MQA or GQA? If MQA, the fused projection layout must map to our optimized attention path. Also need per-head-dim check.

alex: It's MQA: 64 heads, head_dim 128. Export uses fused qkv projection names (qkv.weight -> fused_qkv). Please validate mapping.

priya: Running config validator now with: 
```
rw-validate-model --model s3://rw-models/zh-30b/int_v1/ --checks weights,tokenizer,rope,kvcache,sliding-window --format json --out /tmp/val_zh30b.json
``\Should we also run a generation smoke at 8k tokens?

jamal: I'm on sliding-window tests. Note runtime default stride is 1024 for continuous-batching; for dense Chinese text, smaller stride (512) reduces overlap artifacts. Testing both.

infra-bot: CI pipeline started: validate/zh-30b-int_v1 #601

jamal: Validation summary (local run):
- weights: OK (sha256 matched)
- tokenizer: WARN -> ASCII vs fullwidth punctuation causes ~0.7% prefix mismatch in corpus
- rope: MISSING config -> export has rope_scale=1, no interp metadata
- kv-cache dims: OK (heads=64, head_dim=128)
- sliding-window: INFO -> default stride 1024, suggest 512 for >4k docs
Full log: /tmp/val_zh30b_601.log

priya: For tokenizer warn, could we normalize ASCII punctuation as a preprocessing step in tokenizer wrapper? Maybe add a small normalization map to tokenizer config. That'd be low-risk.

alex: Prefer fixing in tokenizer layer. Jamal, can you add normalizer in tokenizer config like:
```
normalizer:
  ",": "\uff0c"
  ".": "\u3002"
```
and re-run smoke.

jamal: Added local normalizer and ran smoke-gen at seq=8192: 
```
rw-smoke-gen --model s3://rw-models/zh-30b/int_v1/ --prompt tests/long_zh.txt --max-tokens 8000 --batch 1
```
Results: p95 lat ~1.15s/token on a4; memory stable. Up to 4096 tokens outputs match baseline. Around 4096-4120 positions we see small logit diffs when using rope interp (scale=2.0) vs no-interp. Example diffs (top token ids): pos4102 baseline: 412, interp: 415. Small but noticeable.

maya: Expected: interpolation will not be bit-exact. Options: 1) route seq_len>4096 to a long-rope variant; 2) accept small quality delta under threshold. Suggest rollout policy snippet:
```
rollouts:
  - condition: seq_len > 4096
    action: route_to: zh-30b-longrope
    else: continue
```
Can we produce a longrope weights export?

tina: On KV-cache / MQA: jamal, did the optimized attention unit tests pass? Need explicit assertion that per-head ordering and shapes are preserved when mapping fused_qkv -> our kernel inputs.

jamal: Unit tests pass. I also added a KV replay stress test (paste/replay for sliding windows). No crashes. But comparing stride 1024 vs 512 produces ~0.35% token continuation mismatch on beam runs; likely due to different overlapping attention coverage.

priya: Collating action items:
- jamal: commit tokenizer normalizer + update validation -> ETA today
- maya: draft rollout policy + config template for >4k routing -> ETA tomorrow
- tina: add KV-shape assertion to compiled-kernel unit tests -> ETA EOW
- alex: if long-rope variant required, upload weights or confirm not available

alex: Please paste PR when ready. If CI is green we'll canary deploy to dedicated pool tomorrow morning (low-traffic window). Ping me for review. :rocket:

jamal: PR opened: github.com/redwood/infra/pull/3120 (tokenizer normalizer + validation updates). Triggering CI now.

infra-bot: CI result validate/zh-30b-int_v1 #601 -> SUCCESS

priya: Merging and scheduling canary run locally. Will report back with canary metrics.

maya: I'll write a short RFC for the rollout policy and post in #eng-runtime for comments.

alex: Great work. Closing thread; reopen if canary surfaces regressions. :white_check_mark:
